result.topic_en: Title page of Gauss's notebook 'Mathematische Brouillons, October 1805', with scattered notes on quadratic forms over Gaussian integers, a trigonometric problem, astronomical orbital elements, statements on cubic and biquadratic residuacity of 2, and a short Latin deduction about residue characters.

items.english: z is given by z sin(C−B)=a, z sin(A−C)=b, z sin(B−A)=c. One is to find z.

sich unter die Form
$aa+27bb$
setzen lässt so ist
2 Res cub. ipsius $p$
items.english: If a prime p can be put in the form aa+27bb, then 2 is a cubic residue of p.
